member.name: T:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.Grid.GridToolStrip
member.summary:
This class represents a toolstrip which, in general, will be placed directly above a DevExpress XtraGrid control. It uses a custom renderer, GridToolStripRenderer, to mimic the look and feel of the XtraGrid with the Office2003 Paint Style. It includes three standard buttons, a new button, a details button, and a delete button. These three buttons are left aligned on the toolstrip. The GridToolStrip provides three events the containing class can subscribe to to get the three button click events. The tool strip also provides three properties to set the button tool tips.
When placed onto a form the standard toolstrip drop down used to add elements is still available and can be used to place additional buttons onto the tool strip. The general look and feel for additional buttons is that they should be text buttons and right aligned so that the left side of the toolstrip always presents the same buttons.

member.name: M:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.IHotkeyControl.HotkeyPressedInContext(System.Windows.Forms.Keys,TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.IHotkeyControl@)
member.summary: This method tells a particular IHotkeyControl that a key was pressed while it was on the top of the global IHotkeyControl context stack. It should find the IHotkeyControl in it's HotkeyControls list that responds to hotkey and call PressHotkey. The method will return true if it contained a control that accepted hotkey. If the call to PressHotkey sets the newHotkeyContext parameter to true it means that that control wants to become a new context. Therefore that control will be returned as newHotkeyContext, else this reference parameter will be null.
member.param: The hotkey that was pressed
The new context for the hotkey processing.
member.returns: True if this control contained a control that processed the hotkey, otherwise false.

member.name: M:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.IHotkeyControl.PressHotkey(System.Windows.Forms.Keys,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: This method is called to tell the IHotkeyControl that the key hotkey was pressed and the container believes that this control should respond to it. The method will return a boolean value indicating whether or not it was able to process the hotkey. The newHotkeyContext ref parameter will be set to true if the control wants to become a new context.
member.param: The hotkey that was pressed
The new context for the hotkey processing.
member.returns: True if the container believes that this control should respond to the hotkey, otherwise false.

member.name: M:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.IHotkeyControl.ContextPopped
member.summary: This method is called whenver the hotkeycontrol is popped off the current hotkey stack

member.name: M:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.IHotkeyControl.GenerateHotkeyStack(System.Collections.Generic.Stack{TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.IHotkeyControl})
member.summary: Calling this method will start or continue the process of generating a new hotkey control stack. Calling the method with a null parameter tells the hotkey control that it should be the new top context. If it wants to be a context it should create the stack and add itself to it. Then it should find it's parent HotkeyControl and call GenerateHotkeyStack. This process will continue until a top level hotkey context is found at which time it will tell the hotkey message filter to load the new stack.
member.param: The stack of hotkey controls generated by this call.

member.name: T:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.PanelItemProperties
member.summary: This is the base control for all controls needing to provide the Row, Column, NumLines, FixedWidth, FieldBinding, ValidationRule and ToolTipText properties.
member.remarks:
The above mentioned properties are provided through the IExtenderProvider interface so that all child controls of the inheritor will have these properties.
The Row, Column, NumLines, and FixedWidth properties are provided so the flow layout can properly arrange the controls.
The FieldBinding property specifies the table and column(s) the child control needs to be bound to from the data model. The control needing to be bound must inherit the IControlValue interface in order for the data model to set/get the value of the control.
The ValidationRule property sets the validation information so the validation process can validate the changed data before it is updated in the data model.
The ToolTipText property sets the Text that should appear in the tooltip when the user hovers the mouse over the control.

Purpose: Sets the tooltip text specified in the extender provider.

member.name: M:TrueAutomation.Core.Windows.ParagraphControlExt.OnControlValidate(System.Object,System.ComponentModel.CancelEventArgs)
member.summary:
Method: OnControlValidate
Purpose: This control handles the Control.Validating Event
Operation: When the user changes the focus, the Validating event is fired. The framework will validate the value on the control based on validation rules set at design time and appropriately set the IsValid Property on the PanelBaseExtenderProperties for the control.
If the control state has been flagged as invalid, this routine would display an error icon inside the control (right aligned) However if the control state is valid, error icon (if added in the previous editing )would be removed.
The method however would not alter the value on CancelEventArgs.Cancel and retain its default value to false The thinking behind this is not to prevent Focus Change just because the data state on the control is invalid. However this invalid state would be caught when the top level container is validated.
member.param: The being validated.
